object_description: compact three-storey volume with horizontal parapet bands around an inner courtyard
design_condition: the compact volume completes the natural height staggering of the existing campus buildings and forms a new centre, with a free-standing break hall zoning the school path

positive: The compact three-storey volume completes a natural height staggering of the existing buildings
The new building is integrated into the built context and forms a new centre
The break-hall solitaire subtly zones the school path
Routing the garage entrance via the existing parking lot bundles access traffic and frees a green recreation area
The staircase connection from the parking level to the gymnasium level is seen as positive
The main entrance is logically positioned and easy to read
The zenith-lit exhibition space demonstrates an exciting lighting concept for the access courtyard
The sequence of stairs along the inner courtyard is rated positively
Usage units are logically grouped together and promise short distances
Work, school and research rooms are consistently ringed along the facade on all floors
The skeleton structure allows great flexibility for future layouts and changes of use
Floor area, building volume and building costs are in the medium range
Coherent urban design with an ingenious section and consistent core development
negative: The school roof is positioned outside the building lines
The recessed building base with the required fall protection has potential for improvement
The restrained facade supports the horizontality but looks like a conventional office building
Incoherence between the external architectural expression and the interestingly designed interior
The sequence of entrance, core and atrium leads to a cramped situation on the ground floor
The western offices are accessed via a dark corridor zone
The stair landing on the second floor creates a cramped spatial situation
Room proportions are not ideal in all cases
The south-facing column grid in the parking garage is not consistently below the above-ground system
